teile.einleitung: An economic crisis is a time when the economy of a country or of the whole world is doing badly. Companies sell less, people lose their jobs and banks get into difficulty. The best-known crisis is the Great Depression, which began in 1929.
wichtigste: In an economic crisis the economy shrinks and unemployment rises.
The Great Depression began in 1929 with “Black Thursday” on the New York stock exchange.
Switzerland devalued the franc in 1936.
The oil crisis of 1973 came about because Arab OPEC states cut oil production.
The financial crisis from 2007 started in the US market for second-class (subprime) mortgages.
In October 2008 the SNB helped UBS with a stabilisation fund.
In March 2023 UBS agreed to take over Credit Suisse.

abschnitte.text: The economy does not always grow evenly, but in waves. If it shrinks for some time, this is called a **recession**. A particularly severe and long recession is called a **depression**. Typical consequences are companies going bust, unemployment and falling incomes.

On 24 October 1929, **Black Thursday**, share prices collapsed on the New York stock exchange. Many investors lost everything they had. The crisis spread to the whole world, and millions of people were unemployed in the USA and Germany. In Switzerland too, the export industry and tourism suffered, and in 1936 Switzerland devalued the franc so that it could sell more again.

In autumn 1973, Arab states in **OPEC** cut their oil production. As a result, the price of oil rose sharply within a short time. Many countries fell into an economic crisis because energy was suddenly very expensive. In Switzerland there were therefore three car-free Sundays at the end of 1973, on which people went for walks on the motorways.

In the USA, banks had given many people loans for houses that they could hardly pay back. These **subprime mortgages** lost a huge amount of value from 2007. In September 2008 the large US bank Lehman Brothers went bust, and banks around the world panicked. In October 2008 Switzerland rescued UBS: the Confederation gave it money, and the National Bank took bad securities into a stabilisation fund.

Credit Suisse was one of the two big Swiss banks and was founded in 1856 by Alfred Escher. After many scandals and losses, customers withdrew a lot of money in 2023. In March 2023, under pressure from the authorities, **UBS** agreed to take over Credit Suisse. This was meant to prevent a worldwide banking crisis.

States and national banks try to soften crises. For example, they lower interest rates or spend money on building projects. In Switzerland, **short-time working** helps: companies do not have to dismiss employees, and the state pays part of the wages. In the coronavirus crisis of 2020, many Swiss companies also quickly received emergency loans.

begriffe.erklaerung: A time when a country’s economy shrinks.
A marketplace where shares and other securities are traded.
People who want to work cannot find a job.
A loan used to buy a house or a flat.
Employees temporarily work less, and the state pays part of the lost wages.

gewusst: In Europe the term “Black Friday” is often used for the stock market crash of 1929, because owing to the time difference the news only really arrived on the Friday.
During the car-free Sundays of 1973, some people travelled on the motorway by bike, on roller skates or even on horses.
In many countries the Great Depression lasted almost ten years.

teile.einleitung: Checking bills means: you check whether everything on a doctor’s or hospital bill is correct. Health insurers check bills themselves, but insured people should also look carefully. Mistakes are first cleared up with the surgery.
wichtigste: Insured people should check their bills.
You check the date, the name and the treatments charged.
If a treatment is listed that never took place, ask the surgery.
Then inform the health insurer.
Anyone who checks bills helps to save health costs.

abschnitte.text: When **checking a bill**, you look carefully. Are the **name** and **date** of the visit correct? Were all the **treatments** on the bill really carried out? Was anything charged twice? You can also compare the length of a consultation if it is given.

If you find a mistake, first ask at the **doctor’s surgery** or the hospital. Often it is an oversight that is quickly corrected. Then inform the **health insurer**. It can also check the bill and claim back the wrong amount. Keeping quiet is not a good idea, because wrong bills make the health system more expensive for everyone.

**Health insurers** also check every bill themselves, often with computer programs. But they do not know what really happened in the surgery. Only the patients know that. That is why checking by **insured people** is important. In this way everyone helps to keep **premiums** down.

gewusst: Even if the surgery bills the insurer directly, it must give the insured person a copy of the bill so that they can check it.

teile.einleitung: Shopping means getting goods such as food, clothes or school things in exchange for money. Whether at the supermarket, at the market or online, there is a lot to discover when shopping and a few tricks for shopping well.
wichtigste: In a shop you pay at the till.
As proof of your purchase you get a receipt.
A shopping list helps you not to forget anything.
At the market you can buy vegetables directly from the farmer.
Fresh bread is sold at the bakery, meat and sausages at the butcher’s.
At the supermarket you can buy food, drinks and much more.
You carry your shopping home in a shopping bag.

abschnitte.text: In a **supermarket** you find almost everything under one roof: vegetables, milk, bread, drinks and cleaning products. In Switzerland, Migros and Coop are the largest retailers, and there are also Denner, Aldi, Lidl, Volg and many more. You buy fresh bread at the **bakery**, meat and sausages at the **butcher’s**. At the weekly market, farmers often sell their vegetables, fruit and cheese directly.

With a **shopping list** you do not forget anything and you buy fewer unnecessary things. Check beforehand what is still in the fridge at home. Taking your own **shopping bag** is good for the environment. In many Swiss shops, plastic bags at the till cost something, so many people bring their own bag.

You pay at the **till**, with cash, a card or your mobile phone. Many shops also have self-checkout tills, where you scan the goods yourself. As proof of your purchase you get a **receipt**. You should keep it, because without a receipt you often cannot exchange an item or make a complaint.

In the shop it is worth comparing prices, for example using the **unit price** per kilo or litre shown on the price label. Expensive branded products are often at eye level, cheaper ones lower down on the shelf. Sweets are often placed right by the till so that you pick them up on impulse. If you do not go shopping hungry, you usually buy less.

Vegetables and fruit from the region and in season travel short distances and often taste better. In summer, for example, there are strawberries and tomatoes from Switzerland, in winter apples, carrots and leeks. Labels such as the **Bud** (Knospe) of Bio Suisse show that a product has been produced organically. Many farms also sell their products in a farm shop.

In the past, every village had small shops where you were served at the counter. In 1925 **Gottlieb Duttweiler** began selling cheap food from sales vans in Zurich, and this became Migros. Later came self-service shops and large shopping centres. Today many people also order online and have their shopping delivered to their home.

begriffe.erklaerung: A slip that shows what you bought, when and at what price.
Shops that sell goods directly to customers.
The price per kilo or litre, which lets you compare packs.
A shop on a farm that sells its own products.

gewusst: Traditionally, Migros sells neither alcohol nor tobacco in its supermarkets.
In 1925 the first Migros sales vans drove through Zurich with only six products.
The shopping trolley was invented in the USA in 1937.

teile.einleitung: Globus is a chain of department stores in Switzerland that mainly offers beautiful and rather expensive goods. The company was founded in Zurich and still has its best-known store there. If you are looking for fashion, delicatessen or fine gifts, you will find them at Globus.
wichtigste: Globus is a Swiss department store chain based in Zurich.
Its history began in 1892 with a department store run by Josef Weber in Zurich.
In 1907 the company Magazine zum Globus AG was formed.
From 1997 to 2020 Globus belonged to Migros.
In 2020 Globus was sold to foreign investors.
Since 2024 Globus has belonged entirely to the Thai Central Group.
Globus mainly sells fashion, cosmetics, homeware and fine food.

abschnitte.text: Globus is a **department store**, a large shop with many different departments on several floors. You can find clothes, shoes, perfumes, household goods and a large **delicatessen** department there. Globus is aimed at customers looking for special, high-quality goods. There are stores in large Swiss cities such as Zurich, Basel, Bern, Lucerne and Geneva.

In 1892 Josef Weber opened a shop in Zurich called “Bazar ohne Gleichen” (Bazaar without equal). Later the banker Heinrich Burkhardt took over the business. In 1907 it became the **public limited company** Magazine zum Globus. That is why this year is considered the year Globus was born.

In 1997 **Migros** bought Globus for around 700 million francs. For over twenty years the department store thus belonged to Switzerland’s largest retailer. In 2019 Migros decided to sell Globus, because the upmarket department stores did not fit its main business. In 2020 Globus went to a joint company of the Austrian Signa and the Thai **Central Group**.

The best-known Globus store is at Löwenplatz near Zurich’s Bahnhofstrasse. The company moved into this building in 1967. Next to it, on the Papierwerd site on the River Limmat, stands the so-called **Globus temporary building** (Globusprovisorium). This building was really only meant as a temporary solution, but it is still standing today.

At the end of 2023 the Signa group got into serious financial problems. That is why the Central Group from Thailand took over Globus completely in 2024. The Central Group also owns famous department stores in other European countries. For Globus, this means that the company now belongs to a large international department store group.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large shop with many departments where you can buy almost everything.
Especially fine and often expensive foods.
A company divided into many shares that people can buy.
Someone who puts money into a company in order to make a profit.

gewusst: The Globus temporary building in Zurich was only meant as a temporary solution and yet it has been standing for decades.
The first shop from which Globus grew was called “Bazar ohne Gleichen”.

teile.einleitung: Coop is one of the two largest retailers in Switzerland. A large part of the population buys food and everyday items in its supermarkets. Coop is a cooperative based in Basel, and its biggest competitor is Migros.
wichtigste: Coop is one of the largest retailers in Switzerland.
Coop’s headquarters is in Basel.
Coop is organised as a cooperative.
Coop’s big competitor is Migros.
Coop sells many organic products under the Naturaplan brand.
The Coop Group also includes companies such as Jumbo, Interdiscount and Transgourmet.

abschnitte.text: **Coop** runs hundreds of supermarkets all over Switzerland, from small shops to large shopping centres. They sell food, drinks, clothes, cosmetics and much more. The Coop Group employs around 95,000 people (as of 2024) and is one of the largest employers in Switzerland. With the **Supercard**, customers collect points when they shop.

Coop is a **cooperative**, which means that it belongs to its members. Every adult in Switzerland can become a member free of charge. The members elect a council of delegates, which makes important decisions. A cooperative is not primarily meant to make as much profit as possible, but to benefit its members.

In the 19th century, workers in many places founded **consumer associations** so that they could buy more cheaply together. In 1890 these associations joined together to form the Association of Swiss Consumer Societies. In 2001, 14 regional cooperatives merged to form today’s Coop. Since then all the shops have had the same name.

In 1993 Coop introduced the **Naturaplan** brand for organic products. Today Coop is one of the largest sellers of organic food in Switzerland. There are also own brands such as Prix Garantie for cheap products and Fine Food for special delicacies. Many organic products also carry the Bud label of Bio Suisse.

Coop and **Migros** have been big competitors for decades. Both are cooperatives and have a huge network of shops all over Switzerland. One important difference: Coop sells alcohol and tobacco in its supermarkets, while Migros traditionally does not in its own branches. The Coop Group also includes specialist shops such as Jumbo, Interdiscount and Coop City, as well as the wholesaler Transgourmet.

begriffe.erklaerung: Shops that sell goods directly to customers.
A company that belongs to its members and is meant to benefit them.
Products that a shop sells under its own name.
Food produced without chemical sprays and artificial fertiliser.

gewusst: The name Coop comes from the English word “cooperative”.
Coop also owns the majority of Bell, one of the largest meat processors in Europe.
With the Supercard you can exchange collected points for rewards or shopping vouchers.

teile.einleitung: With X-rays you can look inside the body without opening it. Bones show up especially well on them. In this way doctors can see, for example, whether a bone is broken.
wichtigste: X-rays pass through the soft parts of the body.
Bones block the rays more and appear bright on the image.
The rays were discovered in 1895 by Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen.
For this he received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.
X-rays are not without danger, so they are only taken when necessary.
Dentists also often take X-rays.

abschnitte.text: In **1895** the German physicist **Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen** was experimenting with electric tubes. He noticed invisible rays that passed through paper and even through his hand. He called them **X-rays**, because he did not know what they were. In German they are now named after him: Röntgenstrahlen. Doctors started using the discovery soon afterwards.

abschnitte.titel: How an X-ray image is made
abschnitte.text: A machine sends **X-rays** through the body. Behind the body, a sensor or a film catches the rays. Soft parts such as skin and muscles let many rays through. **Bones** block more of the rays and therefore appear bright. In this way the image shows broken bones, but also changes in the **lungs**.

In large amounts, X-rays can harm the body. That is why they are only used when an image is really necessary. Modern machines use very little radiation. Parts of the body that are not being examined are sometimes protected with a **lead apron**. The staff briefly leave the room while the image is taken.

The specialist field for such images is called **radiology**. As well as the simple X-ray image, there is **computed tomography**, CT for short. It uses X-rays to make many cross-sectional images. **Magnetic resonance imaging**, MRI for short, on the other hand works with strong magnets and without X-rays. For the abdomen and heart, **ultrasound** is also often used.

gewusst: X-rays are also used at airports to look inside suitcases.
Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen did not patent his discovery, so that everyone could use it.

teile.einleitung: Solidarity means that people help one another and share burdens together. In health insurance, everyone pays premiums into a shared pot. From this, the costs of the people who are ill at the time are paid.
wichtigste: All insured people pay premiums into a shared pot.
From it, the insurer pays the costs of those who are ill.
In basic insurance, the premium does not depend on your state of health.
Basic insurance has been compulsory for everyone since 1996.
Young and healthy people help bear the costs of older and sick people.
People with little money get a premium reduction.

abschnitte.text: **Insurance** works like a big pot. Many people regularly pay in an amount, the **premium**. When someone falls ill, the insurer pays the costs out of this pot. A serious illness can be very expensive, much more expensive than one person could pay alone. Because many people take part, such costs can be borne.

In **basic insurance**, the insurer does not ask about your health. It must accept everyone. With one insurer, adults in the same region with the same model pay the same amount. There are lower premiums for children and young adults. In this way healthy people help pay the costs of those who are ill.

abschnitte.titel: Why everyone has to take part
abschnitte.text: Since the **Health Insurance Act** of **1996**, every person in Switzerland must have basic insurance. This is called **compulsory insurance**. If the insurance were voluntary, perhaps mainly sick people would take part. Then premiums would rise sharply. With compulsory insurance everyone is protected, and the costs are widely spread.

Older people often need more **treatment** than young people. Even so, adults of all ages pay similar premiums. So young people help pay the costs of older people. Later, when they are older themselves, they benefit from this. This solidarity links the generations.

For some families, premiums are a heavy burden. That is why there is the **premium reduction**. The Confederation and the cantons pay part of the premium for people on a low income. This is also a form of solidarity. Each canton sets the exact rules.

gewusst: With supplementary insurance, the insurer may ask about your health and can also turn people down.
There is a risk equalisation scheme between health insurers so that insurers with many sick customers are not at a disadvantage.

teile.einleitung: Proton is a Swiss company from Geneva that offers encrypted internet services. The best known is Proton Mail, an email service in which nobody except the sender and the recipient can read the messages. The founders met at the research centre CERN.
wichtigste: Proton offers encrypted services such as email, VPN, cloud storage and a password manager.
Proton Mail is an encrypted email service.
The founders met at CERN near Geneva.
Proton Mail started in 2014.
The company is based in the canton of Geneva.
Proton advertises privacy protection and strict Swiss data protection.
Many millions of people worldwide have a Proton account.

abschnitte.text: Proton is a company that offers internet services with strong **data protection**. These include Proton Mail, Proton VPN, Proton Drive for storing files, Proton Calendar and Proton Pass for passwords. Many services can be used free of charge in a simple version. For more storage and features, you pay for a subscription.

Proton’s founders, among them **Andy Yen**, worked as researchers at **CERN**, the large research centre for particle physics near Geneva. In 2013 they talked about how emails could be protected from surveillance. In 2014 they launched Proton Mail. At the beginning the project was financed with money from many supporters on the internet.

In **encryption**, a message is turned into a jumble of characters that seems meaningless. Only someone with the right key can make it readable again. With **end-to-end encryption**, only the sender and the recipient have this key. In this way not even Proton itself can read the emails between two Proton accounts.

Proton stresses that strict laws protecting **privacy** apply in Switzerland. For a long time the servers holding the data were mainly in Switzerland. Even so, Proton also has to obey Swiss laws and help the authorities in certain cases. In recent years there has been debate in Switzerland about new rules on surveillance, which Proton criticises.

Proton has grown from a small project into a large company with hundreds of employees. Since 2024 the majority has belonged to a non-profit **foundation**, the Proton Foundation. This is meant to keep the company independent. Journalists, human rights organisations and people in countries with censorship especially use Proton.

begriffe.erklaerung: A process that changes a message so that only authorised people can read it.
A protected tunnel on the internet that hides your own connection.
Rules that protect personal data from misuse.
A computer that stores data around the clock and makes it available on the internet.

gewusst: Proton was founded by researchers who were actually working on particle physics.
At the beginning, Proton Mail was financed by donations from thousands of people on the internet.

teile.einleitung: Migros is the largest retailer in Switzerland and actually belongs to its customers. Almost every child in Switzerland knows the orange “M”. Migros was founded in 1925 by Gottlieb Duttweiler with five sales vans.
wichtigste: Migros was founded in Zurich in 1925 by Gottlieb Duttweiler.
The logo is an orange “M”.
Migros is organised as a cooperative with over two million members.
In its supermarkets Migros deliberately sells no alcohol and no tobacco.
Migros includes supermarkets, specialist stores, the Klubschulen and the Migros Bank.
With its Culture Percentage, Migros supports culture, education and leisure.
Migros is one of the largest private employers in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: In 1925 **Gottlieb Duttweiler** bought five Ford Model T lorries. These sales vans drove through Zurich offering only six products, including coffee, rice, sugar and pasta. Because he worked without middlemen, his prices were much cheaper. The other shopkeepers were annoyed, but the customers were delighted.

The name comes from French. It lies between “demi” for half and “en gros” for wholesale. The idea is that prices should lie between wholesale prices and normal shop prices. The orange **M** is today one of the best-known signs in Switzerland.

In 1941 Duttweiler turned Migros into a **cooperative**. Since then it has belonged to its members, that is, to many people in Switzerland. Migros is divided into regional cooperatives, for example Migros Aare or Migros Zurich. Members can vote on important questions; in 2022, for example, they voted against selling alcohol in Migros supermarkets.

Duttweiler wanted Migros not only to earn money but also to do something for society. That is why there is the **Migros Culture Percentage**, which supports culture, education and leisure activities. The **Klubschulen** offer courses, for example in languages, cooking or dancing. Parks such as the Gurten in Bern are also part of this.

The Migros Group includes supermarkets, specialist stores such as Do it + Garden, the discounter **Denner** and the Migros Bank. Migros makes many products in its own factories, for example chocolate, bread and drinks. In 2024, for example, it employed around 100,000 people. Many people collect points when shopping with the Cumulus customer card.

begriffe.erklaerung: A company that belongs to its members, who have a say together.
A company that sells goods directly to customers.
Someone who buys goods and sells them on to shops, earning money along the way.
Part of Migros’s money that is spent on culture and education.

gewusst: At the beginning Migros sold only six products, straight from lorries.
In 1941 Gottlieb Duttweiler and his wife gave Migros to its customers.

teile.einleitung: Before going to the doctor, you usually make an appointment. That way the surgery knows when you are coming and can take time for you. Dentists, physiotherapists and many offices also work with appointments.
wichtigste: At most doctors’ surgeries, you make an appointment beforehand.
You can do this by phone and often online too.
If you cannot come, you cancel the appointment in good time.
You take your insurance card with you to the appointment.
In an emergency, you do not need an appointment.

abschnitte.text: Usually the **parents** call the surgery and make an **appointment**. Many surgeries also offer **online booking**. On the phone you briefly say what it is about. Then the surgery knows how much time to plan for. With severe complaints, you can often get an appointment on the same day.

You take the health insurer’s **insurance card** to the doctor’s appointment. For children, the **vaccination booklet** is often useful too. It helps to write down questions beforehand. That way you do not forget anything important at the surgery. Arrive on time or a few minutes early.

Sometimes you cannot keep an appointment. Then you cancel it as early as possible. That way the surgery can give the time to someone else. Many surgeries ask for cancellations at least **24 hours** in advance. Anyone who does not turn up without cancelling sometimes has to pay for the appointment anyway.

abschnitte.titel: When you do not need an appointment
abschnitte.text: In an **emergency**, you do not wait for an appointment. Then you go to a hospital **emergency department** or call **144**. In many regions there is also an emergency doctor number for nights and weekends. For minor complaints you can also ask at the **pharmacy** first.

gewusst: Many surgeries send a reminder by text message or email before the appointment.
Appointments for children’s check-ups are often made months in advance.

teile.einleitung: Roche is a large Swiss group that makes medicines and medical tests. Its headquarters is in Basel, which is also home to its competitor Novartis. At 205 metres, the Roche Tower Building 2 is the tallest building in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Roche has its headquarters in Basel.
The company was founded in 1896 by Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche.
Roche makes medicines and diagnostic tests.
The Roche Tower Building 2 is the tallest building in Switzerland.
Novartis also has its headquarters in Basel.
Roche is one of the largest pharmaceutical companies in the world.
The founding families still hold the majority of the voting rights today.

abschnitte.text: The Basel merchant **Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche** founded the company in 1896. He wanted to make medicines of consistent quality and in large quantities. That was new at the time, because many medicines were still mixed one by one in pharmacies. Roche soon opened branches in other countries.

Roche has two main divisions: **Pharmaceuticals** and **Diagnostics**. In Pharmaceuticals, the company develops medicines, especially against cancer, flu and eye diseases. In Diagnostics, it makes tests and devices that detect diseases in blood or other samples. About 100,000 people work for Roche worldwide (as of 2024).

In Basel there are two white Roche high-rise buildings, designed by **Herzog & de Meuron**. Building 1 opened in 2015 and is 178 metres high. **Building 2** is 205 metres high, was finished in 2022 and is the tallest building in Switzerland. From the side the towers look like a staircase that gets narrower towards the top.

Every year Roche spends many billions of francs on **research**. It often takes ten years or more for an idea to become a finished medicine. New drugs must show in studies that they work and are safe. Roche also owns the American biotech company Genentech, which has been entirely owned by Roche since 2009.

The **pharmaceutical industry** is one of Switzerland’s most important industries. Roche and Novartis are among the most valuable companies on the Swiss stock exchange. They provide thousands of well-paid jobs in the Basel region. That is why Basel is considered one of the most important centres of pharmaceutical research in Europe.

begriffe.erklaerung: The industry that researches and makes medicines.
Examinations and tests used to detect diseases.
A large business with many companies in different countries.
A careful investigation that checks whether a medicine works.

gewusst: The well-known tranquilliser Valium was developed by Roche and came onto the market in 1963.
Before Building 2 was finished, Roche’s Building 1 was the tallest building in Switzerland for a few years.
The name La Roche comes from the founder’s wife, whose surname he added to his own.

teile.einleitung: Rivella is a Swiss soft drink that almost every child in Switzerland knows. What is special about it is an ingredient that comes from milk: milk serum. Rivella has existed since 1952, and the first kind was Rivella Red.
wichtigste: Rivella is a fizzy drink from Switzerland.
Its special ingredient is milk serum.
The first kind was Rivella Red.
Rivella was invented in 1952 by Robert Barth.
The company is based in Rothrist in the canton of Aargau.
Later, kinds such as Rivella Blue and Rivella Green were added.

abschnitte.text: When cheese is made, a yellowish liquid is left over, the **whey**. From this, **milk serum** is obtained, a clear liquid without fat or protein. But it contains minerals and milk sugar. Rivella consists largely of this milk serum, mixed with water, sugar and herb and fruit extracts.

The lawyer **Robert Barth** was looking for a sensible way to use whey. Together with experts, he developed a drink from it. In 1952 it came onto the market under the name Rivella. The name is a reminder of the Ticino village of **Riva San Vitale** and of the Italian word “rivelazione”, which means revelation.

The first kind was **Rivella Red**, with a normal sugar content. In 1959 **Rivella Blue** was added, a version with fewer calories. Later came Rivella Green, with a green tea flavour. Over the years there have been new kinds again and again, for example with peach or rhubarb, some of which disappeared again.

Soon after it was founded, the company Rivella AG moved from Stäfa to **Rothrist** in the canton of Aargau. The drink is still bottled there today. Rivella is a family business and belongs to the Barth family. Besides Rivella, the company also makes other drinks.

Rivella is considered a typically Swiss drink and is very popular at sports events. For many years the company has supported **grassroots sport**, for example running and skiing events. Outside Switzerland, Rivella is known mainly in the **Netherlands**. In most other countries people hardly know it.

begriffe.erklaerung: The liquid that is left over when cheese is made from milk.
Purified whey without fat or protein, but with minerals.
A gas in the drink that makes the fizzy bubbles.
A measure of how much energy there is in a food.

gewusst: Although Rivella is made from milk, it does not taste of milk at all.
In the Netherlands Rivella is so well known that it is on the shelves of many supermarkets.
The name Rivella has nothing to do with rivals, but with a village in Ticino.

teile.einleitung: In uncertain times, investors look for a safe place for their money. They then buy so-called safe-haven currencies. The Swiss franc is one of the best known.
wichtigste: A safe-haven currency is a currency that people seek in a crisis.
The franc is considered a safe and stable currency.
The reason is Switzerland’s political and economic stability.
That is why the franc often rises in value during crises.
A strong franc makes exports more expensive.
The Japanese yen and gold are also considered safe havens.

abschnitte.text: During crises, wars or big stock market crashes, many people worry about their money. They sell uncertain investments and look for something that keeps its value. A currency that is especially in demand at such times is called a **safe-haven currency**. People also speak of a **safe haven**. Like a ship in a storm, the money looks for a sheltered place.

abschnitte.titel: Why the franc of all currencies?
abschnitte.text: Switzerland is considered **politically stable**. It has a long tradition of democracy and neutrality. Its economy is also strong, and compared with many countries the state has little debt. Prices in Switzerland usually rise slowly. That is why many investors from all over the world trust the **franc**.

When many people buy francs, demand rises and so does its **value**. That is nice for holidays abroad, because you get more for your money. But it is difficult for the **export industry**. Swiss products become more expensive abroad and sell less well. That is why the Swiss National Bank sometimes steps in and buys foreign currency to weaken the franc.

Besides the franc, the **Japanese yen** is also considered a safe-haven currency. The **US dollar** is often in demand too, because it is the most important currency in the world. **Gold** is also very popular. It has been used as a store of value for thousands of years. But no investment is completely without risk.

gewusst: During the financial crisis from 2008 and the euro crisis that followed, the franc rose sharply.
Because the franc was in such demand, the National Bank introduced a minimum exchange rate against the euro in 2011.

teile.einleitung: Logitech is a company that makes computer mice, keyboards, webcams and other devices for computers. It was founded in the canton of Vaud in 1981 and is known all over the world today. Perhaps there is a Logitech mouse on your desk too.
wichtigste: Logitech makes computer accessories, for example mice, keyboards and webcams.
The company was founded in Apples in the canton of Vaud in 1981.
Logitech became famous above all for the computer mouse.
Its founders were Daniel Borel, Pierluigi Zappacosta and Giacomo Marini.
Logitech has its official headquarters in Lausanne and an important head office in California.
With the Logitech G brand, the company also makes devices for gamers.

abschnitte.text: Logitech develops devices that you use to operate a computer or to talk to other people. These include **computer mice**, keyboards, webcams, headsets and loudspeakers. Many products work wirelessly by radio or **Bluetooth**. Most of the devices are made in Asia.

In 1981 the Swiss Daniel Borel and the Italians Pierluigi Zappacosta and Giacomo Marini founded the company. The first office was in an old farmhouse in **Apples**, a village in the canton of Vaud. The three had met at Stanford University in California. The company soon began to make computer mice.

When computers came into many offices and homes in the 1980s and 1990s, everyone needed a mouse. Logitech became one of the largest makers of mice in the world. In 2008 Logitech sold its **billionth** mouse. Later came wireless mice, webcams and keyboards.

Under the **Logitech G** brand, the company sells gaming mice, steering wheels and headsets for video games. With Ultimate Ears, portable loudspeakers are also part of the range. During the coronavirus pandemic many people worked from home, so demand for webcams and headsets rose sharply. Today Logitech also makes equipment for video conferences in offices.

Although much of the work takes place in the USA and Asia, Logitech is entered in the commercial register in Switzerland. The company has an important centre at **EPFL** in Lausanne, the Federal Institute of Technology. Its shares are traded on the Swiss stock exchange and on the Nasdaq exchange in New York. Logitech is considered one of the most successful technology companies with Swiss roots.

begriffe.erklaerung: A small device you use to move the pointer on the screen.
A small camera for video calls on the computer.
A radio technology that connects devices without cables over short distances.
Headphones with a built-in microphone.

gewusst: Logitech began in a farmhouse in a small village in Vaud.
By 2008 Logitech had already sold a billion computer mice.

teile.einleitung: Raiffeisen is a group of banks in Switzerland that are organised as cooperatives. This means that the banks do not belong to rich shareholders but to their members, that is, to many quite ordinary people from the region. The first Raiffeisen savings bank in Switzerland was founded in 1899 in the small village of Bichelsee in the canton of Thurgau.
wichtigste: The Raiffeisen banks belong to their cooperative members.
The first Raiffeisen savings bank in Switzerland was founded in Bichelsee TG in 1899.
The name goes back to the German Friedrich Wilhelm Raiffeisen.
The group has its headquarters in St Gallen.
Raiffeisen is one of the largest banking groups in Switzerland.
Many Raiffeisen banks are at home in villages and small towns.

abschnitte.text: In the 19th century many farming families had hardly any money and could not get loans from banks. The German **Friedrich Wilhelm Raiffeisen** (1818 to 1888) therefore had an idea: the people of a village pool their savings and lend them to each other. This is how the first **loan societies** came about. The motto was roughly: what one person cannot manage alone, many can.

The priest **Johann Evangelist Traber** brought the idea to Switzerland. In 1899 he founded the country’s first Raiffeisen savings bank in **Bichelsee** in the canton of Thurgau. Many other villages soon followed, especially in eastern and central Switzerland. Later the individual banks joined together to form a common association.

Each Raiffeisen bank is its own **cooperative**. Anyone who buys a share certificate becomes a member and may have a say at the general meeting. Every member has one vote, no matter how much money they have. The umbrella organisation is called **Raiffeisen Switzerland** and is based in St Gallen.

Raiffeisen offers savings accounts, payment accounts, cards and app banking. **Mortgages**, that is, loans for buying a house or a flat, are especially important. Raiffeisen is one of the largest providers of these in Switzerland. The group has about two million members (as of 2024).

Many Raiffeisen banks support clubs, village festivals and sports events in their region. With the **museum pass**, members get free entry to hundreds of Swiss museums. Because Raiffeisen is so important for the economy, the group is considered **systemically important**. This means that it has to meet especially strict rules.

begriffe.erklaerung: A business that belongs to its members, who make decisions together.
A paper with which you become a member of a cooperative.
A large loan to buy a house or a flat.
So important that its collapse would harm the whole economy.

gewusst: Raiffeisen banks exist not only in Switzerland but also in Germany, Austria and many other countries.
At the general meeting, the vote of a member with just one share certificate counts as much as any other vote.
The cooperative idea, which goes back to Raiffeisen and Hermann Schulze-Delitzsch, has been part of UNESCO’s intangible cultural heritage since 2016.

teile.einleitung: Our body is largely made of water. Every day we lose water, for example when we sweat and breathe. That is why we need to drink regularly, ideally water.
wichtigste: Water is the best drink for thirst.
It has no sugar and no calories.
In Switzerland you can drink tap water almost everywhere without worry.
Children should drink regularly throughout the day.
In hot weather and during sport, the body needs more fluid.
Sugary drinks contain a lot of sugar and harm your teeth.

abschnitte.text: An adult’s body is made up of about **60 per cent** water. In children, the share is even a little higher. Water carries nutrients in the **blood** and helps to control body temperature. Every day we lose water through sweating, breathing and going to the toilet. We have to replace this water.

In Switzerland, **tap water** is of very good quality. Most of it comes from **groundwater** and **springs**. It is checked regularly. Tap water is cheap and does not have to be transported in bottles. That is why it is also good for the environment.

Drinks such as lemonade, iced tea or fruit juices often contain a lot of **sugar**. Sugar provides a lot of energy, which the body does not always need. It can also encourage **tooth decay**. That is why sugary drinks are something for special occasions. For thirst, **water** and unsweetened tea are better.

How much you need to drink depends on age, the weather and exercise. Experts recommend about **1 to 2 litres** of unsweetened drinks a day for adults. Children need a little less, but should drink regularly. In **hot weather** and during **sport**, you need more. Thirst is a sign that the body needs water.

Anyone who drinks too little often becomes tired and gets a **headache**. Concentration at school suffers too. That is why a water bottle in your school bag is a good idea. Fruit and vegetables also contain a lot of water.

gewusst: Cucumbers and watermelons are made up of over 90 per cent water.
In many Swiss towns there are public fountains that you may drink from.

teile.einleitung: Sometimes the doctor’s surgery, hospital or pharmacy sends the bill directly to the health insurer. Even so, you have the right to see the bill. The surgery must give you a copy of it.
wichtigste: If the surgery bills the insurer directly, this is called tiers payant.
Even then, the insured person must receive a copy of the bill.
This is set out in the Health Insurance Act.
With the copy you can check whether the services charged are correct.
The copy can come on paper or electronically.

abschnitte.text: With **tiers payant**, the surgery sends the bill directly to the **health insurer**. The insurer pays the surgery, and you yourself only pay your own share later. This is common with hospitals and pharmacies. Some doctors’ surgeries also bill this way. The name comes from French and roughly means “the third party pays”.

Even if the insurer pays directly, you must receive a **copy of the bill**. This is required by the **Health Insurance Act**. The copy can come by post or **electronically**. If you do not receive one, you may ask the surgery for it. Every patient may see what has been charged.

With the copy you can **check** whether everything is correct. You can see which treatments and medicines were charged. If something is listed that you did not receive, ask the surgery and inform the insurer. In this way insured people help to find **mistakes** and save costs.

gewusst: The counterpart to tiers payant is called tiers garant: you first pay the bill yourself and get the money back from the insurer later.

teile.einleitung: Kambly is a Swiss company that makes fine biscuits (Guetzli). It is based in Trubschachen, a village in the Emmental in the canton of Bern. Many people know the crispy Bretzeli wafers with which it all began.
wichtigste: Kambly makes biscuits.
The company was founded in 1910 by Oscar Kambly.
It is based in Trubschachen in the Emmental.
Its first product was thin butter Bretzeli made to an old family recipe.
Kambly is still a family business today.
The biscuits are sold to many countries around the world.

abschnitte.text: Kambly bakes sweet and savoury **biscuits**, for example Bretzeli, butter biscuits, chocolate biscuits and snacks to go with drinks. The biscuits are baked in a large factory in Trubschachen. The company pays attention to ingredients such as Swiss butter and flour. Kambly is one of the best-known biscuit brands in Switzerland.

In 1910 the baker Oscar Kambly opened a small bakery in Trubschachen. He baked **Bretzeli** to a recipe of his grandmother’s. The thin, crispy Bretzeli were so popular that the bakery grew bigger and bigger. Later his descendants took over the company, which today is run by the third and fourth generations.

Trubschachen lies in the **Emmental**, a hilly landscape in the canton of Bern. The Emmental is known for cheese, farms and dairy farming. The company is one of the most important employers in the region. It is quite rare for a large factory to be in a small village.

In Trubschachen there is a visitor centre called the **Kambly Experience** (Kambly Erlebnis). There you can taste and buy many kinds of biscuits. You also find out how the biscuits are made. The centre is a popular day out for families and school classes.

Kambly sells its products not only in Switzerland but to numerous countries. The biscuits are especially popular as presents in beautiful tins. The company advertises with its Swiss origins and its **tradition**. So a piece of the Emmental travels as far as Asia and America.

begriffe.erklaerung: A dry, crispy baked treat, also called Guetzli in Switzerland.
A thin, crispy wafer baked in a hot iron.
A company that belongs to a family and is often run by it.
A hilly region in the canton of Bern, known for cheese and farming.

gewusst: The large biscuit factory began with a grandmother’s recipe for Bretzeli.
At the Kambly Experience in Trubschachen you can taste many kinds for free.

teile.einleitung: Sika is a Swiss company that makes products for construction, mainly waterproofing, adhesives and additives for concrete. Its products make sure that no water gets into buildings, bridges and tunnels. Sika became famous with a waterproofing agent for the tunnels of the Gotthard railway.
wichtigste: Sika makes products for the construction industry.
The company is known for waterproofing and adhesives.
Sika was founded in 1910 by Kaspar Winkler.
Sika became famous by waterproofing the Gotthard railway tunnels.
Today its headquarters is in Baar in the canton of Zug.
Sika operates in over a hundred countries.

abschnitte.text: The entrepreneur **Kaspar Winkler** founded the company in 1910. He had invented an agent that is mixed into **mortar** so that it hardens faster and does not let water through. He called this product Sika-1. Later Sika became the name of the whole company.

Around 1918 the **Gotthard railway** was to be electrified. But in the long Gotthard tunnel, water kept dripping from the roof, which was dangerous for the electric lines. With Sika’s agent, the tunnel could be sealed. This success made the company known throughout Switzerland and soon abroad too.

Sika produces **concrete additives**, sealants, adhesives, roofing membranes and floor coverings. Concrete additives make concrete, for example, more liquid, stronger or waterproof. Sika adhesives are also used to glue in windscreens in cars or parts in trains. The products are in tower blocks, bridges, dams and stadiums.

The small company became a **global group** with over 30,000 employees (as of 2024). Sika has factories in many countries so that the products are made close to the building sites. Its headquarters is in **Baar** in the canton of Zug. The company is listed on the Swiss stock exchange and is one of the large companies in the Swiss Market Index.

Sika products were also used for the **Gotthard Base Tunnel**, which opened in 2016. In tunnel building, concrete is often sprayed onto the rock face; this is called **shotcrete**. For it to hold straight away, special additives are needed. So, a good hundred years after its first success, the circle closes at the Gotthard.

begriffe.erklaerung: A layer or agent that keeps water out.
A building material made of cement, sand, gravel and water that becomes rock hard.
A mixture of cement or lime, sand and water used to join stones together.
Concrete that is sprayed directly onto a wall by a machine.

gewusst: In many cars, Sika adhesives hold the windscreen in place.
Sika is over a hundred years old and started out as just a small business.
Sika products have also been used in very well-known structures abroad, for example in large bridges and stadiums.

teile.einleitung: Every treatment by a doctor has a price. How this price is calculated is set by a tariff. Since 1 January 2026, a new tariff has applied in Switzerland for outpatient medical services: TARDOC together with outpatient flat rates.
wichtigste: A tariff sets out how services in the health system are paid for.
Since 2026, TARDOC with outpatient flat rates has applied to outpatient medical services.
TARDOC replaced the old tariff TARMED.
Outpatient means: you go home on the same day after the treatment.
For inpatient hospital treatment there are flat rates per case.
Tariffs are negotiated by insurers and healthcare providers.

abschnitte.text: A **tariff** is a kind of price list. It decides how much an examination, a consultation or a procedure costs. This way everyone pays for the same service according to the same rules. Tariffs are negotiated between the **health insurers** and the **healthcare providers**. Healthcare providers are, for example, doctors and hospitals. The **Federal Council** must approve the tariff structure.

For a long time, the tariff **TARMED** applied to outpatient treatment. It was often criticised as outdated. On **1 January 2026** it was replaced by **TARDOC**. At the same time, **outpatient flat rates** were introduced. That is why outpatient bills have looked different since 2026.

With a **fee-for-service tariff** such as TARDOC, every service is listed individually. Each service has a certain number of **tax points**. The points are multiplied by an amount in francs, the **tax point value**. With a **flat rate**, on the other hand, there is a fixed price for a whole treatment. This is meant to make billing simpler.

**Outpatient** means that you go home after the treatment. **Inpatient** means that you stay in hospital at least one night. For inpatient hospital treatment there are **flat rates per case** under the **SwissDRG** system. With these, the hospital receives a fixed amount for a particular treatment.

gewusst: The tax point value is not the same in all cantons, which is why the same service can cost different amounts.
Every doctor’s bill shows codes that indicate which services were charged according to the tariff.

teile.einleitung: A cash machine is a machine where you can withdraw cash from your own account around the clock. In Switzerland many people simply call it a “Bancomat”. For this to work safely, you need a bank card and a secret number.
wichtigste: At a cash machine you get cash, that is, coins or usually banknotes.
In Switzerland people often say “Bancomat” instead of cash machine.
You need a bank card and the matching secret number, the PIN.
The money comes from your own account at the bank.
You must never tell anyone your PIN, not even friends.
When typing in your PIN, you cover the keys with your hand.
The world’s first cash machine was in London from 1967.

abschnitte.text: A cash machine is a device that gives out money without a bank employee being there. You find them at bank branches, railway stations, shopping centres and airports. In Switzerland it is often called a **Bancomat**; elsewhere people also say ATM, short for “Automated Teller Machine”. Many machines give out banknotes in francs, and some at stations or airports also give out **euros**.

First you put the **bank card** into the slot or hold it against the reader. Then you type in the secret number and choose the amount. The machine checks with the bank whether there is enough money in the **account**. Then first the card and then the money comes out, so that you do not forget your card. The amount is taken from your own account straight away.

The **PIN** is a secret number, usually with four or six digits. The abbreviation stands for “personal identification number”. If you type the PIN in wrongly several times, your card is blocked, often after the third attempt. You should learn your PIN by heart and never write it on the card. Neither the bank nor the police will ever ask for your PIN.

When typing, cover the keys with your free hand so that nobody can watch. Fraudsters sometimes secretly fit card readers or small cameras to machines; this is called **skimming**. If something about the machine looks strange, it is better to choose a different one. If you lose your card, have it blocked by the bank immediately.

The first cash machine was put into operation in London in June 1967, at that time with special vouchers instead of cards. Soon afterwards the machines came to Switzerland too. In the past, you had to go to the bank counter during opening hours to get cash. Today many people pay with a card or mobile phone, so in some countries there are fewer **cash machines** again.

The name Bancomat caught on so strongly in Switzerland that it is used for all cash machines. At your own bank’s machines you can usually withdraw money without a **fee**. At other banks or abroad, withdrawing often costs something. Despite TWINT and cards, many Swiss people still like using cash.

begriffe.erklaerung: Money you can touch, that is, coins and banknotes.
A secret number that shows that the card belongs to you.
A place at the bank where your own money is managed.
Fraud in which card details and PIN are secretly spied on.
A bank card with which the money is taken directly from the account.

gewusst: At the first cash machine in London in 1967, you could only withdraw a fixed amount of 10 pounds.
Many cash machines give out the card first and only then the money, because otherwise many people would forget their card.
The word Bancomat was originally a brand name and then became an everyday word.

teile.einleitung: AMAG is the largest car importer in Switzerland. It mainly brings cars from Volkswagen and other brands of the VW Group into Switzerland and sells them through its own garages and partners. About one in three new cars in Switzerland comes from this group.
wichtigste: AMAG is the largest car importer in Switzerland.
It imports cars of the Volkswagen brand as well as Audi, Škoda, Seat and Cupra.
A car importer brings cars into the country from abroad and sells them.
AMAG was founded in 1945 by Walter Haefner.
The company still belongs to the Haefner family today.
Besides sales, AMAG also offers repairs, leasing and mobility services.

abschnitte.text: AMAG is a Swiss family business that imports, sells and repairs cars. The name is an abbreviation for Automobil- und Motoren AG (Automobile and Engine Company). The company has many of its own **garages** all over Switzerland and works with numerous partner garages. It employs several thousand people and trains many apprentices.

Switzerland does not have a large car industry of its own. That is why all new cars have to be brought into Switzerland from abroad. A **car importer** buys the cars from the manufacturer, brings them across the border and distributes them to the dealers. It also makes sure that the cars meet Swiss regulations.

AMAG’s most important brand is **Volkswagen**, whose cars, such as the VW Golf, are very popular in Switzerland. There are also other brands of the VW Group such as Audi, Škoda, Seat and Cupra, as well as VW Commercial Vehicles. Together these brands are among the best-selling in Switzerland. More and more of these cars are electric.

The entrepreneur **Walter Haefner** founded AMAG in Zurich in 1945. Shortly afterwards he began to import the VW Beetle into Switzerland. In the 1950s and 1960s the Beetle became one of the most popular cars in the country. Walter Haefner lived to be over 100, and today his family continues to run the company.

AMAG does not just sell cars, but also offers **leasing**, insurance and car subscriptions. It builds charging stations for electric cars and solar panels on its buildings. It is also working on car sharing and new forms of mobility. In this way it wants to prepare for a future with fewer petrol and diesel cars.

begriffe.erklaerung: A company that buys goods from abroad and sells them in its own country.
You rent a car for a few years and pay an amount for it every month.
A place where cars are sold and repaired, not just a place to park them.
A company that belongs to a family and is often run by it.

gewusst: AMAG is one of the largest training companies for jobs in the motor trade in Switzerland.
For many years the VW Golf was one of the best-selling cars in Switzerland.
About 240,000 new passenger cars are sold in Switzerland each year (as of 2024).

teile.einleitung: When you arrive at a doctor’s surgery, you are often greeted first by the medical practice assistant. She organises how things run in the surgery and helps the doctor with her work. In Switzerland it is a popular apprenticeship.
wichtigste: The medical practice assistant, MPA for short, works in the doctor’s surgery.
She welcomes patients and takes their insurance card.
She makes appointments and answers phone calls.
She also helps with medical tasks, for example taking blood.
In Switzerland, you learn the job in a three-year apprenticeship.

abschnitte.text: The **medical practice assistant**, **MPA** for short, welcomes patients at reception. She takes the **insurance card** and checks the details. She makes **appointments** and answers the phone. In an urgent case, she helps decide who needs to be seen quickly. In this way she makes sure that everything runs smoothly in the surgery.

The MPA also helps the doctor with treatment. For example, she measures **blood pressure** or takes **blood**. In the surgery’s small **laboratory**, she tests blood or urine. She can also take **X-rays** and put on bandages. She also deals with bills and with invoicing the health insurers.

In Switzerland, you learn the job in a **three-year apprenticeship** with a federal certificate of proficiency, EFZ for short. You work in a surgery and attend vocational school. What matters is enjoying contact with people, being precise and staying calm even in hectic moments. After the apprenticeship there are many kinds of further training.

gewusst: The medical practice assistant must keep everything she learns in the surgery confidential, just like the doctor.

teile.einleitung: Insurance is an arrangement in which many people regularly pay in a small amount. If someone is unlucky, for example falls ill or suffers damage, they get help from this shared fund.
wichtigste: With insurance, many people pay a little so that there is enough for everyone.
The regular amount is called the premium.
Anyone who suffers damage gets money from the shared fund.
Healthy people also pay into health insurance, because everyone can fall ill one day.
There is insurance for many things, for example for your home, your car or your bike.
In Switzerland, basic health insurance is compulsory for everyone.

abschnitte.text: Major damage can be very expensive for one individual. That is why many people join together. Each person regularly pays a small contribution, the **premium**. Anyone who is unlucky gets money from this fund. This is called the **principle of solidarity**: the many help the few who need help at the time.

Imagine every child in the class puts one franc into a box. If a child loses their ball, the class buys a new one with the money. For the individual child the ball would be expensive, but for everyone together it is not much. This is exactly how **insurance** works. Nobody knows in advance who will be affected, but everyone is protected.

In Switzerland, every person who lives here must have **basic insurance** with a health insurer. This is set out in the Health Insurance Act, **KVG** for short. Healthy people also pay premiums, because nobody knows when they will fall ill. For children, the parents usually pay the premium. That way there is money when someone needs to go to the doctor or to hospital.

There is insurance for almost everything. **Household contents insurance**, for example, pays if something is stolen at home, including a bike. **Liability insurance** pays if you accidentally break something that belongs to someone else. For cars, liability insurance is compulsory. The **AVS** is also an insurance: it helps in old age.

Anyone who takes out insurance signs a **contract**. It states what the insurance pays for and how high the premium is. Often you have to pay part yourself when there is damage. Some insurance is voluntary, other insurance is required by law. It is worth reading the conditions carefully.

gewusst: Hundreds of years ago, merchants were already joining together to protect themselves against the loss of ships and goods.
Compulsory basic health insurance has existed in Switzerland since 1996.

teile.einleitung: Brushing your teeth keeps them healthy and protects against holes. Anyone who brushes properly and regularly needs treatment at the dentist less often.
wichtigste: You brush your teeth at least twice a day.
Ideally in the morning and in the evening.
One brushing takes about two minutes.
An egg timer or a song helps you keep to the time.
Toothpaste with fluoride strengthens the teeth.
A well-known order is KAI: chewing surfaces, outer surfaces, inner surfaces.

abschnitte.text: You brush your teeth **at least twice** a day, in the morning and in the evening. Brushing before going to sleep is especially important. At night, less **saliva** flows, which otherwise protects the teeth. One brushing takes about **two minutes**. A small egg timer, a timer or a song helps you keep going for that long.

So that you do not forget a tooth, you brush in a fixed order. Many children learn the **KAI method**, from the German words for the three surfaces. First come the **chewing surfaces**, in other words the surfaces on top of the back teeth. Then you brush the **outer surfaces** with small circles. Finally come the **inner surfaces**, which face the tongue.

A **toothpaste with fluoride** makes tooth enamel stronger against acid. There is special toothpaste with less fluoride for children. You only need a small amount, about the size of a pea. You do not swallow the toothpaste but spit it out. With small children, the parents brush again afterwards.

The brush cannot reach everywhere between the teeth. **Dental floss** or small interdental brushes help there. Eating few sweet things and drinking plenty of water also protect the teeth. Regular check-ups at the **dentist** show whether everything is in order. In many Swiss schools, an expert from the school dental service shows how to brush properly.

gewusst: Many bacteria live on the tongue, so you can gently clean it too.
Milk teeth are important even though they fall out: they keep the space free for the permanent teeth.

teile.einleitung: The exchange rate tells you how much one currency costs in another currency. If you go on holiday to Italy, you have to change francs into euros and need the exchange rate to do so. It changes almost every second.
wichtigste: An exchange rate is the price of one currency in another currency.
If 1 euro costs 0.95 francs, then you need exactly 190 francs for 200 euros.
If the franc becomes stronger, holidays abroad become cheaper for Swiss people.
A strong franc makes Swiss products more expensive abroad.
Banks earn money on the difference between the buying rate and the selling rate.
Exchange rates come about through supply and demand on the foreign exchange markets.

abschnitte.text: An **exchange rate** works like a price label for money. It tells you, for example, how many francs you have to pay for one euro or one US dollar. If 1 US dollar costs 0.80 francs, then for 50 francs you get exactly 62.50 dollars. So you calculate 50 divided by 0.80.

Today most currencies are traded freely. If many people and companies want to buy francs, its price rises and the franc becomes stronger. The franc is considered a **safe haven**, so investors buy it especially in times of crisis. Interest rates and the mood on the financial markets also influence the rate.

If the franc becomes stronger against the euro, you get more euros for the same amount of francs. This makes holidays in Italy, France or Spain cheaper. On the other hand, Switzerland becomes more expensive for tourists from abroad. Hotels in the Alps notice this through fewer guests from Europe.

Switzerland sells many goods abroad, for example watches, machines and medicines. If the franc is strong, these **exports** become more expensive abroad and harder to sell. In return, goods from abroad, the **imports**, become cheaper for Swiss people. That is why the Swiss National Bank watches the exchange rate very closely.

Banks and bureaux de change have two rates: a **buying rate** and a **selling rate**. They buy euros from you more cheaply than they sell euros to you. They earn money on this difference. That is why you always get a little less when changing money than the official rate given in the news.

From 2011 to 2015, the Swiss National Bank set a **minimum exchange rate** of 1.20 francs to the euro. On 15 January 2015 it surprisingly removed this minimum rate. The franc became much stronger within minutes. This event is called the franc shock.

begriffe.erklaerung: Money held in another currency, for example euros in a bank account.
A currency becomes stronger and is worth more than before.
A currency becomes weaker and is worth less than before.
A counter where you can change money into another currency.

gewusst: Currencies worth several trillion dollars are traded every day on the world’s foreign exchange markets.
In the past many exchange rates were fixed; the franc has only floated freely since 1973.
If you pay by card abroad, you are also changing money, you just do not notice it directly.

teile.einleitung: The economic cycle is the name for the ups and downs of the economy: sometimes things go well and many people find work, sometimes things go badly and companies sell less. These rises and falls repeat themselves like waves. Experts watch them closely in order to spot crises early.
wichtigste: The economic cycle describes the ups and downs of the economy.
A typical economic cycle has the phases recovery, boom, downturn and depression.
If real GDP falls for two quarters in a row, people often speak of a technical recession.
Stagflation means a stagnating economy with high inflation at the same time.
Kondratiev cycles are long waves of about 40 to 60 years.
The KOF at ETH Zurich publishes a well-known economic barometer every month.
The debt brake requires income and spending to balance over an economic cycle.

abschnitte.text: The **economic cycle** shows how strongly the economy is growing or shrinking at the moment. This is measured mainly with **gross domestic product**, GDP for short, the value of all goods and services produced in a country. When GDP rises, the economy is usually doing well. When it falls, there are fewer orders and often more unemployed people.

An **economic cycle** consists of recovery, boom, downturn and depression. In the recovery, production and employment rise. In the boom, companies are working at full capacity and prices often rise sharply. In the downturn, demand weakens, and in the depression, the low point, unemployment is at its highest.

A **recession** is a fall in economic output. If real GDP falls for two quarters in a row, people speak of a technical recession. **Stagflation** is especially difficult: the economy stands still and at the same time prices rise sharply, as in many countries in the 1970s. The biggest crisis of the 20th century was the Great Depression from 1929.

In the 1920s the Russian economist Nikolai Kondratiev described long waves in the economy. These **Kondratiev cycles** last about 40 to 60 years. They are often linked with great inventions, such as the steam engine, the railway, electricity or the computer. Whether these waves really exist is disputed among experts.

The British economist John Maynard Keynes recommended that the state should spend more or cut taxes in a recession. This **counter-cyclical fiscal policy** is meant to support demand. In good times, the state should save instead. For this, Switzerland has the **debt brake**, which the people accepted by a large majority in 2001 and which requires income and spending to balance over a whole cycle.

The **KOF Swiss Economic Institute** at ETH Zurich publishes the KOF Economic Barometer every month, which is meant to show how things will develop over the coming months. The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs SECO also makes regular forecasts. The Swiss economy depends heavily on exports, so it feels crises in Europe or the USA quickly. One example was the sharp slump in 2020 during the coronavirus pandemic.

begriffe.erklaerung: The value of all goods and services a country produces in a year.
A phase in which economic output falls.
A high phase in which the economy is running very strongly.
The economy standing still while prices rise at the same time.
A rule that the Confederation may not spend more than it takes in over the long term.

gewusst: Some experts even look at sales of lorries or packaging, because they show early whether the economy is picking up.
Switzerland’s debt brake later served as a model for other countries such as Germany.
The German word for economic cycle, Konjunktur, comes from the Latin “coniungere”, which means to join.

teile.einleitung: In a stock split, one share is divided into several new shares. The price becomes smaller, but the value of what you own stays the same. Companies do this to make their share easier to handle.
wichtigste: In a stock split, each share is divided into several new ones.
In a 1 to 2 split, you get two new shares for one share.
The price roughly halves.
The value of your stake in the company stays the same.
The aim is a cheaper share that is easier to handle.

abschnitte.text: Imagine a pizza that is cut into 8 slices. If you cut each slice in two again, you have 16 slices. But the pizza has not got any bigger. A **stock split** works in exactly the same way. In a split **in the ratio 1 to 2**, you get two new shares for each share. The **price** of each share roughly halves.

You own 10 shares at 200 francs each. Together they are worth 2000 francs. After a 1 to 2 split, you have 20 shares at about 100 francs each. That is 2000 francs again. Your **stake in the company** has stayed exactly the same size. There are just more shares, and each one is worth less.

If the price of a share has risen very high, a single share becomes expensive. It is then harder for small investors to buy it. After a split, a share is cheaper and **easier to handle**. This can make trading easier. The opposite also exists: in a **reverse split**, several shares are combined into one, and the price rises accordingly.

gewusst: A split does not make anyone richer or poorer. It only changes how the value is divided up, rather like changing a 100-franc note into two 50-franc notes.
Ratios such as 1 to 10 or 1 to 20 are also possible.

teile.einleitung: Anyone who is very ill or seriously injured goes to hospital. Doctors, nurses and many other experts work there day and night. You can stay overnight in hospital until you feel better again.
wichtigste: In hospital you are looked after day and night.
There are different departments, for example for emergencies or children.
The family may come during visiting hours.
With small children, parents can often stay in hospital.
Basic insurance pays for the general ward.
The canton pays a large part of the costs of a hospital stay.

abschnitte.text: A **hospital** is a place where sick and injured people are treated. Unlike a doctor’s surgery, you can also stay overnight there. There is an **emergency department**, operating theatres and rooms with beds. Doctors, **nurses**, therapists and many other experts work together. For children there are separate **children’s hospitals** or children’s wards.

Anyone in hospital is pleased to have **visitors**. Family and friends may come during **visiting hours**. With small children, parents can often even stay overnight in the room. This makes the child feel safe. In hospital you have to be considerate, because other people need rest.

Many hospitals offer a **general**, a **semi-private** and a **private** ward. **Basic insurance** pays for the general ward. There you often share a room with others. The medical treatment is equally good in all wards. Anyone who wants a single room or a free choice of doctor needs **supplementary insurance**.

A stay in hospital is expensive. For inpatient treatment, the **canton of residence** pays at least 55 per cent of the costs. The health insurer covers the rest. Adults also pay a small **hospital contribution** per day. Children and young adults in education or training are exempt from this.

In Switzerland there are small regional hospitals and large central hospitals. The five **university hospitals** are in Zurich, Bern, Basel, Lausanne and Geneva. Particularly difficult illnesses are treated there. They also train doctors.

gewusst: The word “Spital” comes from the Latin “hospitalis”, which means hospitable.
Many children’s hospitals have hospital clowns who make sick children laugh.

teile.einleitung: Work is everything people do to make something, to help or to earn money. Adults often work in a job and get paid wages for it, but cooking, cleaning and helping at home are also work.
wichtigste: Adults work, among other things, to earn money.
The money you get for your work is called wages.
A lot of work such as cooking and cleaning is done at home without pay.
The place where you work is called the workplace.
Anyone who works for a company is an employee.
Children can help at home, for example by laying the table.
The end of the working day is called knocking-off time.

abschnitte.text: Work means making an effort to reach a goal. The baker bakes bread, the teacher teaches, the doctor cares for the sick. Work for which you get paid is called **paid work**. There is also housework and **voluntary work**, for example in a sports club or the fire brigade. All these kinds of work are important for a society to function.

Anyone who works for a company is **employed** and receives **wages** every month. With their wages, families pay for rent, food, clothes and holidays. Other people are **self-employed** and run their own business, for example a hairdresser’s or a farm. An employment contract states how much you work and how much you earn for it.

The **workplace** can be an office, a workshop, a hospital, a shop or a tractor in the field. Some people also work from home on the computer, and this is called working from home. In Switzerland, full-time employees usually work about 40 to 42 hours a week. After work comes **knocking-off time**, the free time in the evening (in German “Feierabend”).

Cooking, washing, cleaning, shopping and looking after children are a lot of work, even if nobody pays wages for them. In Switzerland, this **housework and family work** adds up to even more hours than paid work. Children can help, for example by laying the table, tidying their room or watering the plants. If everyone in the family helps, there is more time left for things to do together.

In Switzerland, the **Labour Act** sets out how long people may work at most and what breaks are needed. Employees are entitled to at least four weeks’ holiday a year, and young people up to 20 to five weeks. **Child labour** is forbidden. Young people from 13 may only do light work, for example delivering newspapers or helping in the garden.

In the past, most people worked in farming, but today most work in the service sector. Machines and computers take over a lot of hard or monotonous work. In return, new jobs are created, for example in **computing** or in care. That is why it is important to keep learning new things all your life.

begriffe.erklaerung: The money you get for your work.
Work for which you are paid.
Work that you do without pay for others or for a club.
The free time after the end of the working day.

gewusst: In Switzerland, more unpaid work is done every year than paid work.
The German word “Feierabend” originally meant the evening before a church holiday.
A great many adults in Switzerland volunteer, for example in clubs or helping neighbours.

teile.einleitung: Emmi is the largest milk processor in Switzerland. The company from Lucerne turns milk into cheese, yoghurt, butter and milk drinks. Some of its cheese even matures in a sandstone cave.
wichtigste: Emmi is the largest milk processor in Switzerland.
Emmi mainly processes milk.
Emmi’s headquarters is in Lucerne.
Emmi lets some of its cheese mature in a sandstone cave in Kaltbach.
The company is mostly owned by dairy farmers from central Switzerland.
Well-known products are Emmi Caffè Latte, Kaltbach cheese and yoghurts.

abschnitte.text: **Emmi** buys milk from thousands of farms and turns it into many different products. These include cheese, yoghurt, cream, butter, quark and milk drinks. Emmi has its headquarters in Lucerne and factories in Switzerland and many other countries. About 9000 people work for the company worldwide (as of 2024).

Emmi was formed in 1907 when **dairy cooperatives** in central Switzerland joined together. The farmers wanted to sell and process their milk together. To this day, the majority of Emmi belongs to an organisation of central Swiss milk producers. Some of the shares are traded on the stock exchange.

In **Kaltbach** in the canton of Lucerne there is a natural sandstone cave. It is cool and damp all year round, ideal for maturing cheese. Emmi stores tens of thousands of cheese wheels there, for example Emmental and Gruyère. In the cave the cheese gets a special flavour and a dark rind.

Especially well known is **Emmi Caffè Latte**, a coffee drink with milk in a cup. Emmi also makes many well-known Swiss cheeses, including Emmental, Le Gruyère and Appenzeller. There are also yoghurts, desserts and plant-based products without milk. Many products are exported to over 60 countries.

Emmi owns companies in the USA, Spain, Italy, Brazil and other countries. There it makes, for example, goat’s cheese or Italian desserts. For Swiss dairy farmers, Emmi is one of the most important buyers. The company is also committed to **animal welfare** and more climate-friendly milk production.

begriffe.erklaerung: A company that makes cheese, yoghurt and other products from raw milk.
The time during which cheese is stored and develops its flavour.
A rock made of sand grains pressed together.
An association of people who pursue a goal together.

gewusst: Emmental cheese is famous for its large holes, which are formed by gases from bacteria during maturing.
A cow in Switzerland gives more than 20 litres of milk a day on average.

teile.einleitung: An investment means spending money today in order to get a benefit or more money in the future. A baker buys a new oven, a municipality builds a school, and a state builds a tunnel. Whether an investment is worthwhile can be checked with various calculations.
wichtigste: In an investment you use money today in order to have a benefit later.
If an old machine is replaced by an equivalent new one, this is called a replacement investment.
The payback period shows after how many years the money used has flowed back.
A positive net present value means that the investment earns more than the discount rate.
The internal rate of return is the interest rate at which the net present value is exactly zero.
Depreciation spreads the loss in value of machines over several years.
Net investment is gross investment minus depreciation.

abschnitte.text: An **investment** is spending on something that is used over a longer period, for example machines, buildings, vehicles or computers. Money for research or further training can also be an investment. Companies invest in order to produce more or better. Private individuals invest, for example, in education, a flat or **shares**.

In a **replacement investment**, an old machine is replaced by an equivalent new one. In an expansion investment, more is bought, for example a second van to serve more customers.
